title: Elevated Energy Prices Add to Fed’s Dilemma on Interest Rates
partialText: Investors now expect that the Fed will delay a rate cut until September instead of July, as they had before the war in Iran began.

title: New Supreme Leader Inherits Sprawling, Secretive Office That Dominates Iran
partialText: His father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, had turned what was traditionally a religious affairs office into a shadowy national security juggernaut.

title: War Brings New Water Crises to an Already-Parched Iran
partialText: Iran has accused the United States of bombing a desalination plant on Qeshm Island. The country was already facing a severe water shortage.

title: Trump Antisemitism Inquiry Demanding List of Jews at Penn Heads to Court
partialText: The Trump administration, which said it is investigating harassment, sued the University of Pennsylvania after it refused a request to provide information about Jewish students and staff.

title: D.C. Bar Begins Disciplinary Proceedings Against Ed Martin
partialText: A new legal filing accused Mr. Martin, a senior Justice Department official, of an unethical pressure campaign against Georgetown University.

title: Kennedy to Undergo Rotator Cuff Surgery
partialText: The secretary of health and human services, known for his Make America Healthy Again campaign, is expected to be back at work on Monday.

title: Mississippi and Georgia Elections: What to Watch in Today’s Primaries
partialText: It’s Primary Day in Mississippi, where a younger Democrat is trying to oust a House veteran, and in Georgia, where Marjorie Taylor Greene’s former seat is up for grabs.

title: Democrats Sued to Find Out Whether Trump Will Send Armed Officers to Election Sites
partialText: In a lawsuit filed Tuesday, the D.N.C. sought to compel the government to say whether it plans to deploy armed federal officers in this year’s elections.

title: Alexander Brothers Found Guilty on All Counts in Sex-Trafficking Trial
partialText: The verdict comes more than a month after the trial began in Federal District Court in Manhattan where the jury heard weeks of emotional and often graphic testimony.

title: San Francisco Bay Area Residents Weigh Possibility of BART Reductions
partialText: The Bay Area Rapid Transit system was once so successful, it could rely mostly on riders to sustain itself. But the pandemic dealt BART an unusually heavy blow.

title: Noma Loses American Express and Blackbird Sponsors For Los Angeles Dinners
partialText: Two companies have withdrawn from a series of dinners in Los Angeles after The Times reported allegations that René Redzepi attacked workers.

title: At Noma, Accusations of Past Physical Abuse
partialText: Dozens of former employees say René Redzepi inflicted physical and psychological violence on the staff for years.

title: The Race to Stop Wildlife Trafficking in Africa
partialText: In Nigeria, customs officers and conservationists are confronting the grim impacts of the $20 billion trade.

title: Michelle Pfeiffer, With Mixed Feelings, Is Busier Than Ever
partialText: At 67, the actress is still reinventing herself, with two new TV shows, “The Madison” and “Margo’s Got Money Troubles,” and an evolving attitude about her work.

title: iPads in Kindergarten, YouTube on Breaks: The School Screen-Time Battle
partialText: Mounting evidence shows that excessive computer use can harm children, so parents are cutting back at home. Now, the debate has shifted to the classroom.

title: Mamdani Chooses His Words Carefully After Alleged Terror Attack
partialText: Mayor Zohran Mamdani has been spare in his remarks following the attempted bombing at Gracie Mansion and arrests of two men who said they were motivated by ISIS.

title: Who Are the Men Accused of Bringing Homemade Bombs to Gracie Mansion?
partialText: A high school senior and a recent graduate, both from the Philadelphia suburbs, were charged by federal prosecutors with trying to support a terrorist group.

title: Review: A New ‘Tristan und Isolde’ at the Metropolitan Opera
partialText: Yuval Sharon’s debut production featured an astonishing performance by the soprano Lise Davidsen. It is the event of the season.

title: I Asked a Former Trump Official to Justify This War
partialText: Nadia Schadlow, a deputy national security adviser during Trump’s first term, explains how the U.S.-Israel war with Iran fits in with an “America first” agenda.

title: Trump Has No Idea How to End the War With Iran
partialText: Only when the U.S.-Israeli bombing of Iran comes to a halt, without destroying the state, can the Iranian people sort out their fate.

title: War and the Economy
partialText: We look at the conflict’s global economic impact.

title: Tell Us About Your Plans for a Longer Life
partialText: If you are saving money and have a plan for the future, we want to hear how it’s going and any advice you have for others.

title: Dozens of States Weigh Continuing Live Nation Antitrust Case
partialText: After the Justice Department reached a settlement with the concert giant, the judge overseeing the trial asked the states and the company to do the same.

title: USA Today Names Jamie Stockwell as Next Top Editor
partialText: Ms. Stockwell, who recently left The Washington Post, is the third person named to the job in the past three years.

title: In Ancient Peru, a Parrot Trade That Crossed the Andes
partialText: Scientists studied centuries-old bird feathers from an ancient tomb on the coast, and then traced the origins back to the Amazon.

title: The Killing Of Haiti’s President Heads to a U.S. Court. What to Know.
partialText: Four men are accused in South Florida of plotting to kill President Jovenel Moise in 2021. His death plunged Haiti into chaos that continues today.
